metadata.title: Cauliflower Buffalo Wings Recipe
metadata.description:
Hi Guys, today I’m going to make Cauliflower buffalo wings or bites with cauliflower. This is one beautiful bunch of cauliflower. I’ll show you how to cut it up. 
Wash the cauliflower and remove the outer leaves. Cut the stem off. Remove all of the green parts. Cut the florettes by going around the cauliflower. Cut them into bite size pieces like this. Always cut the cauliflower from the stem, push your knife down and split. The flowers naturally split without breaking apart. 

Link to my cast iron pan:  http://amzn.to/1A0wfV7
Link to strainer:  http://amzn.to/1IBsxCL

In my bowl, I’m adding 1 cup of all purpose flour, 1 tsp onion powder, 1 tsp garlic powder and ½ tsp salt. Mix this. Add about ½ cup to 3/4 cups water to make a nice batter.

I’ve heated up vegetable oil in my cast iron pan. I try to avoid frying things but in this case, frying is the only way to get the cauliflower really crispy. Baking it results in a soggy texture and that’s not what we want for these crispy bites. Put a drop of the batter into the oil. If it floats to the top quickly like this, it means your oil is hot and ready. Leave the heat on medium. 

Into my batter, I’ll put the cauliflower and toss them around. Drop them into the hot oil one at a time. Don’t overcrowd the pan. 

In the meantime, mix ¼ cup hot sauce and 2 tbsps melted butter in a cup. I like Frank’s hot sauce but you can use any brand that you like. 

Fry the cauliflower until golden brown like this. Transfer to a bowl using a slotted spoon which helps drain the oil. You can hear how nice and crispy they are. Make sure to get all the small particles out of the oil so they don’t burn when you fry the next batch. 

I’ve found that it’s best not to put the cauliflower directly into the hot sauce mixture because that makes it soggy. Drizzle on a few teaspoons of the hot sauce mixture and toss thoroughly. This way, the cauliflower stays crispy. I’ll taste it. mmmmm, it’s absolutely perfect. It has just the right amount of hot sauce for me. Like with any fried food, it’s best served immediately. Otherwise, it will get soft and defeat the purpose of frying. Hear that, that’s how crunchy it is. It’s totally worth the frying. You can serve this with the traditional blue cheese dressing or yogurt.

I hope you’ll try this recipe. Don’t forget to subscribe and thanks for watching!

summary.brief: A woman chops cauliflower, coats it in a seasoned batter, fries the pieces, tosses them in a hot‑sauce butter glaze, and plates them with a side sauce and garnish.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a whole head of cauliflower on a wooden cutting board. The woman in a red shirt removes the outer leaves and stem, then cuts the head into bite‑size florets. She places the florets in a bowl and mixes a batter of all‑purpose flour, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, and water until smooth. After heating vegetable oil in a cast‑iron pan (testing the heat by dropping a bit of batter, which rises quickly), she tosses the cauliflower pieces in the batter and drops them into the hot oil one at a time, using tongs to turn them and a slotted spoon to lift them out when they turn golden brown. The fried bites are drained in a bowl to remove excess oil. Meanwhile she melts butter and mixes it with hot sauce in a separate cup. She drizzles a few teaspoons of this hot‑sauce‑butter mixture over the crispy cauliflower and tosses gently with a spoon so the coating stays crisp. Finally she plates the tossed cauliflower on a white plate, accompanied by a small bowl of white sauce and a garnish of green leaves; a portion of the bites has already been eaten.

You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to either of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   A video can match neither, one, or both. Be strict — when in doubt,
   say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
